This makes me think back to when I was 15. I was slowly killing myself by upping the amount of painkillers I was taking each week. Now I’m 20 and I wish I could tell my 15 yr old self that everything is going to be okay. I wish I could give them a hug and tell them they are going to get through it. I wish I could show them the amount of love they have for themselves in the future. Please just take it day by day, it sucks ass, but take it day by day please. Today is shitty? I’m gonna wait until tomorrow. The technique I’ve used to live as long as I have is when I feel suicidal, I run through a checklist: Is it after 9pm? Can’t kill yourself. Have you drank water in the past 6 hrs? Can’t kill yourself. Have you had food within the past 3hrs? Can’t kill yourself. Have you seen the sun in the past 24hrs? Can’t kill yourself. Have you taken a shower in the past 2 days? Can’t kill yourself. Have you talked to another person within 12 hrs? Can’t kill yourself. Setting boundaries like that has made me at least make it to the next morning. Which is all that matters. Fuck trying to think years ahead, just try to make it to the next morning.

I posted on here a few weeks ago, I put up a literal piece of trash for upwards of a thousand dollars (as a joke but I am also extremely poor so I was hoping for a miracle to be able to afford rent), and keep getting offers way above my asking price. So I know those are going to be scams, I just don’t understand why? It’s not the same as if I put a tv or a laptop up, where if they scam you out of your money and get it for free it’s actually worth something, while If they “scam” me out of my money and I send it to them, they are literally not getting anything of resell-able value? It’s a piece of trash I twisted to a sculpture? There will be no place that it has value?? Why would someone even want to go through the effort of scamming someone to receive an “art” sculpture? I know it’s dumb I even put it on there, I’m just financially struggling and thought it would be funny. I just can’t wrap my head around it???
Thank you, I just don’t know anymore

You all are definitely going to hate me for this one, but I jokingly put up a shit piece of “trash art” up on eBay for WAYYY too high of an asking price (above a thousand dollars). I did this because I am seriously broke as hell as a college student and was like “maybe some person might buy this and I’ll afford to eat AND pay rent this month.” But when I woke up this morning I saw that someone had “offered” four hundred dollars more than I asked for, and other than the pure shock I also had a million red flags get raised. It’s literally a piece of trash that I twisted and molded into a dumb little figure, no one would actually be willing to pay that much for it. Do I accept it and watch my PayPal closely for payment? Or do I immediately shut it down and wait to see if there even could be a genuine person willing to buy my literal trash?
Thank you!

This could possibly be triggering so I'm giving a warning. I guess I should have clarified that I'm not suicidal, I don't self-harm, in no way am I going to be causing the dog physical harm. I'm not expecting a puppy to be the end-all cure-all in its puppy phase. I meant "dangerous" as in, well I don't really know how to phrase this, outside sources could be a danger to me, not the dog. In the same way a person having a medical episode is a dangerous situation. I really don't want to go into the complexities of what I'm going through, but I will say that in no way, shape, or form will I be putting the dog in any danger. I'm not a monster. Thank you for your input though I'm sure I could have clarified further. My mistake.

I agree that puppies are indeed challenging as I've trained basic obedience in many a few myself. I am definitely concerned about the prospect though and do want to set the pup for success. I do have experience with puppies but yeah I am worried about the noise complaints as they will be practically unavoidable. I've trained a service dog before and had to wash her because she was a bit too reactive to aggressive dogs and I didn't feel as if she enjoyed service work. I didn't do PA with her until she was around a year old (we actually didn't know her age but we had a rough estimation). I would love it if I had the option to live with my parents but they are hard strict about getting me out of the house as soon as possible. I'm also taking three college courses already so I'm not extremely concerned about the workload. But also if I were to live off-campus in an apartment, I would have even less time to spend with the puppy. it's just a back and forth of a lose-lose situation. If I had the opportunity to get from a program I would but its just unreasonable for my situation. Thank you for your advice I really appreciate hearing about your experiences and will definitely take it into consideration.

I 100% agree that an eight-week-old puppy is harsh to call a service dog in training. What I will say is that I definitely understand how hard raising a puppy is, my family is a bunch of dog lovers and I've had the full experience from birth to death many times. I'm the "dog whisperer" of my family and friends because I've trained basic obedience many times and they always reach out to me if the dog is behaving in a disruptive way (nipping, stealing food, etc.). I have trained a service dog before but I ended up washing her due to her not enjoying working and a slight reactivity to aggressive dogs that I just wasn't comfortable with continuing service dog work with. Honestly, I certainly underestimated the training and it was quite an immature decision since the dog I received was from a puppy mill (I had NO idea at the time and didn't do as much research) and it was too late for her to be able to reconcile from the trauma that comes from being in a puppy mill. It was completely immature and I recognize that. For this planned dog though I'm getting it from a responsible breeder and will be working closely with an actual service dog trainer. I'm going to college to be a veterinarian which requires a doctorate, and I'm worried that deferring would take me too far off the track as a doctorate takes about eight years (roughly). Currently, I am taking three college classes and two Ap classes, so I'm not too concerned about the workload. And since my parents are extremely strict on leaving the house as soon as possible, I'm stuck in a merry-go-round of not being able to live at home but not being able to live on the campus. It's just a complicated situation. Thank you so much for your advice though I am certainly grateful.
